sections.trivia:
First Old Firm Ne'erday game since 1969.
An unchanged side for Celtic.
Murray, who was attempting a comeback after retiring from persistent foot injuries, played neither in the Reserve or main game. Sean Fallon said that this was due to the heaviness of the grounds and not to some relapse. 
On the Tuesday before this game Celtic defeated Rangers 2-1 in a Reserve League match at Celtic Park. The Celtic team was Hunter, Gourlay, Baillie, Hannah, Aitken, Casey, McCluskey, Glavin, Hood, Burns, Wilson. Subs Ritchie and Innes. The Celtic scorers were Hood and O'Hara o.g.
sections.review:
Rangers scored on the half hour when McLean swung over a cross from the right and Johnstone outjumped the Celtic defence to head home.
Celtic's defence always looked vulnerable at crosses although they should have equalised in the second half after Sean Fallon replaced his strikers Deans and Lennox with Hood and Wilson.
In the last part of the game Celtic went close on a number of occasions although Dalglish was well shackled by Hamilton first then O'Hara. Without Kenny's creativity Celtic found it hard going.
Remarkably, even with the loss, Celtic stayed top of the league. Now Rangers were snapping at the heels but their form looked as suspect as Celtic's. The attempt to make the league "more open" – ie. change the rules so that Celtic did not win it each year – looked to have succeeded.

sections.trivia:
Steve Murray returns to the team as a sub after announcing his retirement in September with a toe injury.   
  This was future Celtic manager Gordon Strachan's first apperance as a player at Parkhead.  
  Motherwell announce that the cup tie against Celtic on 24 January is all ticket with a limit of 30,000.
sections.review:
Celtic blew a two goal lead on a bitterly cold day at Parkhead.
At 3-1 Celtic looked home and dry with Deans and Dalglish in fine form and Dundee having defenders Stewart and Caldwell withdrawn through injury and replaced. However the defence still looked suspect and Dundee scored twice to grab an impressive point in their struggle against relegation.
The disappointment around Celtic Park is palpable. The Ne'erday loss to Rangers followed by this 'collapse' when in a winning position meant that there was something underlying the performances fundamentally wrong.
Sean Fallon lambasted his defence and rumours abound that Celtic are after a new centre half with Ian MacDonald of St Johnstone and Alan Hansen of Partick Thistle both being mentioned in the press.

sections.review:
Motherwell are having their best season for years so this was a huge result for Celtic.
There were many positives on the day. Deans scored twice, hit the bar and set up Dalglish's goal near the end to clinch it. Edvaldsson played sweeper behind MacDonald and McCluskey as the full backs pushed forward.
But the biggest boost was the return of Steve Murray to the midfield. He organised the team in the centre of the park and together with Ronnie Glavin they ran the game and allowed Dalglish to move into the forward line where he is most dangerous.

sections.trivia:
St Johnstone were rock bottom of the new Premier League.
The rerorganised team with Murray, Glavin and Lennox that had played against Motherwell started again.
Jock Stein returned to hospital during the week for a further operation on his injuries sustained in the care crash that kept him out as manager and Sean Fallon in charge of matters on the field. There was also talk of Stein moving upstairs into a general manager's role at Celtic Park.
Dixie Deans had his two front teeth knocked out but bravely played on until the end. He does not know if he spat them out or swallowed them.
On the same day Celtic lost 2-0 to St Johnstone in a Reserve League match at Celtic Park. The Celtic team wsa Connaghan, Gourlay, Baillie, Hannah, Aitken, Casey, McCluskey, Wilson, O'Donnell, Burns, Hood. Subs Little and Innes. Henderson scored both of St Johnstone's goals.
Celtic were drawn against FC Sachsenring Zwickau in the quarter finals of the European Cup Winners Cup. The first round would be at home.
sections.review:
Relegation bound Saints gave their best performance of the season but three times Celtic came back from a goal down to win.
17 – Lambie scores a fine goal after combining with O'Rourke and the ball goes in off a post.
23 – Celtic equalise when Deans backheels Edvaldsson's pass into the path of Dalglish who beats two men and scores with a fine left foot shot.
33 – Thomson scores with a spectacular 30 yarder after Glavin gave away possession in midfield.
45 – Deans equalises after he outjumps MacDonald to a Lynch cross.
46 – Saints in front again after referee Paterson gives a soft penalty for Lynch's tackle on Hotson. Latchford saves Thomson's penalty but Crammond scores the rebound.
70 – Roddy MacDonald scores with a header following a corner to level again.
89 – With only seconds remaining Edvaldsson grabs a dramatic winner with a spectacular flying header.

sections.review:
Motherwell came back from 2 goals down to record a dramatic victory in a jam packed Fir Park.
Celtic were strong favourites after their 3-1 win on the same ground 14 days earlier. They were 2-0 up in 39 minutes but a second half defensive collapse cost them dear.
Dalglish opened the scoring with a magnificent rocket shot free kick from 25 yeards in 31 minutes and Andy Lynch scored the second 8 minutes later.
After half time Motherwell manager Willie McLean threw caution to the wind and by 61 minutes Bobby Graham and Ian Taylor had them level.
The winner came in 70 minutes when Willie Pettigrew chased a long ball through the middle and outpaced a static Celtic defence to fire a shot into the net off a post. The goal was a disaster for the Celtic defensive pairing of McDonald and McCluskey.
Celtic fought for an equaliser but the goal would not come. This was the first time Celtic had been knocked out in the 3rd round since 1968 and was a severe blow to caretaker manager Sean Fallon.

sections.trivia:
Ally Hunter is recalled in goals. This was his last ever appearance for Celtic. With the aftermath of the Cup game against Motherwell, all positions were looked at again. Latchford, being found wanting found himself out.
As well as Latchford dropping out, Roddie MacDonald was dropped along with Ronnie Glavin and Bobby Lennox. In came Andy Ritchie, Tommy Callaghan and Paul Wilson.
On the Wednesday the Celtic team had been taken to the BBC studios to view their last matches and review the defensive lapses. Archie McPherson recalls this in his biography of JHock Stein saying how Stein berated them.
During the week Brian McLaughlin went out on loan to Finn Harps in Ireland.
sections.review:
Fallon rings the changes after last week's cup debacle at Fir Park. The changes were made and the importance of a win was paramount having lost in the Scottish Cup, surrendered the League Cup and seemingly faltering in the League.
Poor Ally Hunter, recalled after a year out of the side, lost a soft goal to a Henry Hall shot in the first minute. Celtic fought back well with youngster Andy Ritchie having a great first half in midfield and Paul Wilson scored the winner on his return with a fine volley. Tom McAdam had a goal for Dundee Utd disallowed for offside just before the interval.
This was an important win at a crucial stage.
At the end of a challenging month Celtic still lead the Premier League

Steve Murray was back in training after a recurrence of the toe injury. Jackie McNamara would be out for a month with an injury.

sections.review:
When Dalglish plays to the full then Celtic are on form and he scores two excellent goals to give Celts victory.
In the first half Celtic made chances but Cruickshank was in inspired form and made four tremendous saves.
After the break Celtic brought McCluskey back to sweeper and pushed young Casey into midfield and Celtic had more drive.
Dalglish opened the scoring in 59 minutes with a cute lob after Deans had knocked down a McCluskey free kick. Near the end Dalglish clinched it when he headed in a fine cross from Ritchie. Dalglish now described as 'Captain Marvel.'
Youngsters Ritchie and Casey played well on the day with Ritchie impressing with his powerful shooting.

sections.trivia:
A major stooshie broke out in the press, all hair-curlers, house coats and outrage, when an article written by Jackie McNamara and published in 'The Leveller' magazine in December came to light. McNamara, who made no disguise of his leaning towards the Communist Party, said in the article that football "…. was a sick and horrible business" whilst stating a number of truths about the game, it's running and other matters.
As the 14th was a Scottish Cup Fourth Round weekend, Celtic had an off weekend. Sean Fallon headed to Ireland on another scouting trip. As an aside John Clark was at the club working as a first team coach at this time.
Kenny Dalglish played as an overage player for the Scotland U23 team against the Netherlands on the 18th February. Scotland lost 2-0.
Roy Aitken makes his Celtic league debut at centre half.
On the same day Celtic lost 3-2 to Aberdeen in a Reserve League match at Celtic Park. The Celtic team was Connaghan, Gourlay, McGrane, Hannah, McDonald, Innes, Mackie, Hood, McCluskey, Callaghan, Temperley. Subs McGrain and Little. The Celtic scorers were Temperley and Callaghan.
sections.review:
Celtic dominated but couldn't break through. The turning point came in 75 minutes when Davie Robb smashed a shot off the bar in front of goal.
Celtic's goal came minutes later when Dalglish beat three men and chipped the ball to the back post for Lennox to deftly head home.
Roy Aitken impressed greatly on his Celtic debut at centre half.

sections.trivia:
Sachsenring manager Karl Heinz Kluge watches from the Parkhead stand. Celtic had the information on Sachsenring from an English referee David Mitchell who had reffed their previous European game against Panathinaikos. Sean Fallon announced he would not go to East Germany to watch Sachsenring in advance of the game. 
Dalglish was fit having overcome a leg injury sustained in the game against Aberdeen.
On the Friday it was reported that Celtic would take on Anglo-Scot Jimmy Smith on loan from Newcastle Utd for at least a month and that he would arrive on the following Tuesday prior to thew European game. Smith had undergone 3 cartilage operations and there were questions as to his fitness. By the Monday Smith was having second thoughts about reporting to Celtic Park.
Both Ritchie and Casey were out with 'flu. The strain of 'flu doing the rounds was catching out a number of teams with Partick Thistle close to postponing their Saturday game.
  Deans scores his 20th goal against Hibs in a Celtic jersey. This one was his last against the Hi-Bees.
sections.review:
Celtic blitzed Hibs with a first half treble on a windy day.
Dixie opened the scoring with his usual goal against Hibs this time from the penalty spot after Lennox had been brought down in the area. He then set up Lennox for the second goal. Wilson adeed the third following up on a Dixie shot that rebounded from a post.
The best goal was kept until the second half when Dalglish played a one-two with Deans, looked up and curled a glorious shot past Hibs' keeper McDonald.
At the end of the month Celtic had stolen a lead having played a game more.

sections.trivia:
FCV Zwickau also known as BSG Sachsenring Zwickau. Played at the Westsachsenstadion.
Celtic hit by flu bug before the game. Glavin, Ritchie and Casey are out and Wilson played with a temperature of 102 degrees.
Celtic had prepared as normal at Seamills with all the flu victims missing and away from the squad. Harry Hood stepped in for Ronnie Glavin. Hood had spent a lot of the season as either a sub or with the Reserves.
Upper stand was all ticket only.
Bobby Lennox missed a penalty.
Celtic had 21 corners to Sachsenring’s one.
Celtic take Newcastle midfield star Jimmy Smith on trial with a view to signing him. The deal had been set up for Smith to join on the Tuesday but on the Monday he got cold feet about joining Celtic. He arrived on the day of this game.
Celtic were looking at signing Johnny Doyle from Ayr Utd with a transfer deadline then set at March 16th.
sections.review:
Celtic attacked from the start and in 2 minutes Croy missed a Dalglish cross but Lynch blazed his shot over the bar.
Celtic had constant possession as the German side retreated into a defensive shell. In 22 minutes Celtic were awarded a penalty when Dalglish was fouled in the box but Croy made a magnificent one handed save from Lennox’s penalty high to his right.
Celtic broke through in 40 minutes when McGrain created an opportunity for Dalglish to score with a low shot.
After the break Celtic continued to press and Dalglish slid a shot wide from a fine Hood-Lennox move. Then the fans despaired when Dalglish skied a shot over from only three yards out.
Celtic began to get frustrated and with only two minutes left Blank slipped past Aitken, the 17 years old Celtic centre back, and raced through to score past Latchford.
At full time the Sachsenring players did cartwheels of Joy on the Parkhead turf. Celtic players had given their all with Dalglish an outstanding talent on the night and the result was a total injustice.

sections.trivia:
Celtic had been due to face Ayr Utd on the Saturday 6th and Rangers on the 13th before but the matches were postponed with the 'flu bug hitting all teams. Celtic's game previous to this had been the home leg and they had been without a game for two weeks other than a practise match against the Reserves.  
This was Celtic's first and last visit to the old East Germany and they were based in the city of Karl Marx Stadt.   
  Celtic have injury/flu crisis with Lynch, Ritchie, George McCluskey, Deans and Lennox all missing, Latchford, McGrain, Dalglish Wilson, Casey and Glavin just recovered   
  Because of flu Celtic could only name four subs.   
  John Doyle signed from Ayr United at Glasgow airport for £90,000 and travelled with the team although he could not play.   
  Edvaldsson wears number 9 shirt but plays in defence.   
  Celtic had to complete documents to 'adopt' 17 year old defender Roy Aitken to allow him entry into East Germany.   
  STV transmit the game back live to Scotland with an early afternoon 2pm kick off, despite the protests of managers and jobsworths up and down the country saying there would be a spate of grannies funerals, four hour 'flu and dental appointments   
  The Scottish League lost 1-0 at Hampden to the English League later on this day.  
  Sachsenring lost 5-0 to Anderlecht on aggregate in the semi finals.
Outside of football, Harold Wilson caught the country out and resigned as Prime Minister and leader of the Labour Party.
sections.review:
Sean Fallon played Roddy MacDonald as an emergency striker due to an injury crisis.
Celtic suffered a blow when Blank scored after only three minutes with a fine shot over Latchford from 20 yards after outpacing McCluskey.
Celtic found their feet and had almost all the play. Before half time there was a flurry of chances when Hood shot over, MacDonald deflected a Dalglish back heel past the post and then Hood again fired wide.
In 57 minutes Celtic missed their best chance. A powerful Glavin shot was parried by Croy and MacDonald lost his balance with goal gaping.
In 86 minutes there was controversy when MacDonald headed in a Hood corner but the referee blew for an infringement and the last chance was gone.
Celtic could argue that they were unlucky over both legs. A sad end to St Patrick's day 1976.

Kenny Dalglish is single handedly keeping Celtic ahead in the title race.
Roddy MacDonald is played as a striker with Deans, Lennox and Glavin all out injured. He does well in this unusual role.
Dalglish adds to his catalogue of great goals when he beats two men and places the ball calmly past Allan. McGrain set up the goal with a great run through the centre of the Dundee defence.

sections.review:
United are playing for their lives and fight for every ball. A strong wind and bare park also make it a difficult day to bring the ball down and pass.
McAdam's goal near half time was crucial and left Celtic chasing the game. Dalglish equalised with a 25 yard shot but Hall and McAdam made it 3-1 with young Aitken's inexperience in defence now showing.
Dalglish scored with three minutes left to make a fight of it and he had hit the bar earlier. Despite his goals Kenny didn't have his best game but he had virtually no support on a day when Celtic did not perform.
The Celtic fans left in a black mood and now realised that they had lost the initiative in the league race to Rangers.Top of the tabel changed with Celtic losing and Rangers winning

sections.review:
Celtic's old foe, referee JRP Gordon, comes to the fore again.
With minutes remaining Bobby Clark had possession and rolled the ball out too far. Dalglish anticipated and nipped in to steal possession and tuck the ball home for the winning goal. There was no infringement on the goalie and the linesman ran to the centre circle to give the goal but Gordon, who was 20 yards away and looking at his watch, ran back to award a free kick to Aberdeen much to the disgust of the Celtic players and fans.
Sean Fallon commented afterwards that 'Aberdeen may have had only 10 men but they had other advantages….'
Young red head Tommy Burns impressed on his full debut but Aberdeen had 10 men for 44 minutes and Celtic could not breach them.
Dalglish's goal came from the usual supply of McGrain making a good run on the right and crossing into the box. Aberdeen scored when Edvaldsson attempting to clear a free kick hooked the ball past Latchford.
In the second half Miller was sent off and Aberdeen had a goal disallowed for a foul. And at the death JRP ruled out the Dalglish goal.
Aberdeen stayed up on goal difference at the end of the season and this point was invaluable to them.

Near the end the big Celtic support belted out 'You'll never walk alone' in pure defiance but at the final whistle they left in near silence.

sections.from_'portsmouth_news'_newspaper::
Celtic last night ruthlessly underlined the warning Ian St John had issued in recent weeks – that Celtic don't play friendlies.
The mighty Glasgow side crushed heir hosts in an entertaining match at Fratton Park- but a match where the edge was always showing.
Only briefly when the Scots had cruised into an early two goal lead did the Celts ease off slightly and by half time they might have been caught.
They must have caught a blast from manger Jock Stein for there was no slacking in the second half as their silky skills tore a re-jigged Pompey apart and brought four more goals.
It was in fact a devastating and delightful display of skillful soccer and one which deserved more an audience of more than 9279.
That is perhaps the saddest thing about it – the net gate for this match after Celtic's small fee and expenses was £4500. Not the sum to keep the looming financial wolf from Pompey's door.
That is carping; the night which produced it was a night when skills predominated. Despite the size of the scoreline it was not a night without hope for Pompey.
There was a fighting display from Chris Kamara who underlined the tremendous potential Pompey have unearthed. There was also a fine 45 minute display from Phil Figgins who must surely be number one choice for goalkeeper next season.
The night also highlighted the inherent problem in the side, the absence to finish off what is created.
Although on the receiving end for long periods Pompey still managed to create openings yet they rarely managed to force Scottish – Anglo keeper Peter Latchford into action.
Figgins' hard work started in the 13th minute when he had a fine parry from the delicately, deadly Kenny Dalglish.
Two minutes later he was beaten as a long, hopeful through ball from Pat McCluskey caught the defence without cover and little John Doyle whipped away to hit home his first senior goal since his recent £90,000 move from Ayr United.
Two minutes later Figgins brilliantly beat away a fierce cross shot from Paul Wilson but in the 26th minute defensive uncertainty between Paul Went and Peter Ellis let the menacing Bobby Lennox in to accept a gift golden chance.
It convinced Celtic they were in easy street as they became casual and over complex and Pompey, working hard, forced their way into the game in the 31rst minute as Micky Mellows effectively tucked away Bobby McGuinness's pass.
For the rest of the half Celtic were under pressure and in the last minute Latchford just managed to beat away a fierce Steve Foster shot after a goal mouth scramble.
It changed after the interval, Celtic were now playing for real and Pompey's hopes of holding the Scottish giants were destroyed by two goals in three minutes.
Grahame Lloyd, who had replaced Figgins, had already made a great ave from the aggressive Ronnie Glavin when the dark haired midfielder popped up to make it 3-1 after Wilson's shot had came crashing off the woodwork.
That was in the 61rst minute and seconds later Lloyd made another great save from Glavin. In the 64th minute substitute defender Roy Aitken linked with to race through a flat footed defence to make it 4-1.
Quickly Pompey might have pulled one back but McGuiness's shot merely ended in the side netting after Latchford merely palmed away a cross from substitute Billy Eames. In 70 minutes, Dalglish, the man whose goal beat England on Saturday, underlined his rare ability with a devastating goal. Taking a pass from Wilson just outside the area he spotted Lloyd off his line and with deadly delicacy chipped it just under the bar.
Glavin was still thundering through looking for goals and was still being foiled by Lloyd. Then in 78 minutes manager St John allowed sentiment to rule and he brought 17 year old Celtic worshiper Paddy McParland as sub and the little Scot's first touch looked a goal until a defender deflected it away.
The last word lay with Celtic and another substitute, George McCluskey, profited from a moment's hesitation by Lloyd to force home the sixth.
A lesson to learn – St John
Pompey came in for withering criticism after game from manager Ian St John.
'Celtic were terrific, absolutely terrific, and I'm delighted the match went that way.'
'It may prove to some of my big time Charlie's the level they are playing at and how much they have to learn.'
'Before the match some of them knew nothing about Scottish football but they weren't prepared to,listen to me.'
'I told them Celtic would work had, come down here to win – perhaps they have learned a lesson tonight.'
'Too many of my players thought they were doing me a favour coming in and training for this match but Celtic had world class players out there willing to play as if it were a cup final.'
'Look at Danny McGrain. On Saturday he played against England, he played again on Moday night yet at the death tonight he was willing to race the length of the field just to link up the play – that's the kind of attitude you have to have.'
'Obviously we are disappointed at the gate, you get people who will travel 500 miles and others who won't come round the corner.But those who stayed away were the losers. This was tremendous entertainment.'
'I didn't expect people to come and see us I thought they would come to see Celtic. I'm sure those who did are glad they took the trouble. That was a world class performance.'
